item.title: Incarico post-doc: IpD48/2026: Extracellular Vesicles from Engineered Microalgae for the Sustainable Delivery of Ketocarotenoids and Tocopherol in Advanced Cosmetic Applications (Univ. VERONA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-09 13:00
Institution: Univ. VERONA, Verona
Field: Biology / 05/BIOS-07 Biochimica

The researcher will carry out experimental activities within the ALGAVES project, aimed at developing extracellular vesicles (EVs) derived from engineered microalgae as delivery systems for ketocarotenoids and tocopherol. Activities will include EV isolation and purification and their characterization by NTA, TEM, DLS and Western blot. The researcher will contribute to bioactive compound quantification by HPLC and to EV uptake studies in HaCaT keratinocytes by confocal microscopy. Antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects will be assessed through ROS and redox status. item.description:
Deadline: 2026-10-30 23:59

item.title: Incarico post-doc: Targeting MAcrophage metabolism to Reduce aggressiVE Liver metastases (MARVEL) ref. D.R. 126/2026 (HUMANITAS University)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-05 12:00
Institution: HUMANITAS University, Pieve Emanuele - Milano
Field: Biology / 05/BIOS-08 Biologia molecolare

MARVEL aims to develop novel therapeutic strategies to tackle liver metastases from pancreatic and colorectal cancer by modulating macrophage functions within the tumor microenvironment. The project focuses on two key processes: the recruitment of circulating monocytes and the metabolic reprogramming of liver-resident macrophages, which contribute to establishing an immunosuppressive environment that supports metastatic progression.

item.title: Incarico post-doc: Integration of microbiological, molecular, and bioinformatic methodologies for the epidemiological and environmental monitoring of viral pathogens and antibiotic resistance in wastewater. (Univ. PERUGIA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-10-28 23:59
Institution: Univ. PERUGIA, Perugia
Field: Biology / 05/BIOS-15 Microbiologia

The research project aims to develop and implement microbiological and molecular methodologies, such as qPCR/dPCR and next-generation sequencing, and to integrate them with bioinformatic and biostatistical analyses to investigate emerging and re-emerging pathogens and antibio tic-resistant bacteria in wastewater. The project involves applying this experimental ap proach to specific case studies to obtain epidemiological information regarding the preva lence of pathogens and antibiotic resistance in the population, as well as to evaluate the potential environmental impact risk of treated wastewater.
